# Intake Brief: Follow-on-Steam incentive — unlock a bundled free game in the Steam launcher

## Problem statement

The upcoming Steam release of the Tableau Card Engine launcher (Electron) needs a growth mechanic: when a player follows the game/developer on Steam, they receive one of the bundled example games for free. The mechanic must feel seamless — the Steam store page opens automatically (player already logged in), they follow, and the launcher detects the follow and unlocks the bonus game.

## Users

- **Steam players** — get a free game as an incentive to follow the TCE Steam presence; discover the engine's games.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — grow Steam following/wishlists and reward engaged players without manual key distribution.

**User stories:**
- As a Steam player, I want to click "Follow us on Steam" in the launcher and have the store page open automatically (already logged in), so following takes one click.
- As a Steam player, I want the bonus game to unlock in my launcher once I've followed, so I can play it immediately.
- As a publisher, I want the free-game unlock to be delivered through the existing bundled-content/DLC architecture, so no manual key handling is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The launcher shows a "Follow us on Steam" call-to-action (e.g. a small panel/button) that opens the game's Steam store page in the Steam client/overlay via Steamworks (player is already logged in — no browser login prompt).
2. After the player follows, the launcher detects the follow via Steamworks and unlocks the designated bonus game (one of the existing example games) in the launcher's game list; verified by an end-to-end check with a real Steam account (manual QA) and, where feasible, a mocked Steamworks session in automated tests.
3. The unlock persists across launches (player who followed once keeps the game; no re-verification prompt on every boot).
4. The bonus game is delivered as part of the bundled-content architecture (locked by default) so no separate download is needed; the unlock mechanism is game-agnostic (works for whichever game is designated as the bonus).
5. If the Steam client/Steamworks is unavailable (e.g. dev environment, non-Steam launch), the launcher must not crash: the CTA degrades gracefully (hidden or "follow via browser" fallback) and the web app remains fully functional.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` must succeed (quality gate).

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Electron** launcher per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW; this feature integrates Steamworks SDK into that launcher (explicitly deferred scope of the launcher item — this item introduces it).
- **Bonus game is bundled** (answer to intake Q: "a game currently in the example games", delivered via the bundled/subset content in the launcher, unlocked in place) — not a separate download.
- **Steam store page via Steamworks** (intake Q3): the CTA opens the store page in the Steam client; follow detection must use the Steamworks SDK and/or Steam Web API.
- **Licensing:** all code MIT-compatible; no proprietary or copyleft dependencies.
- **Quality gates:** `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass before pushing (project policy).
- **Doc-update policy:** infra/tooling changes require `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` updates (or a tracked child work item).
- **Game-agnostic:** the unlock logic must not hard-code the specific bonus game title (the designated game is a business decision, see Appendix).

## Existing state

- Launcher item CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (intake_complete) delivers the Electron binary that boots the Vite web app; scope explicitly defers Steamworks SDK integration ("No Steamworks SDK integration in v1. The launcher must not require Steam to run locally during development.").
- Launcher content-loading is designed so Steam DLC directories can be read (option a) with structure permitting later Steamworks-managed paths (option b) without a rewrite — the follow-unlock must slot into this abstraction.
- The web app (Game Selector) currently lists all example games; the launcher will bundle a subset.
- No Steamworks SDK, Steam app ID, or Steam-related code exists in the repo today.

## Desired change

1. Add Steamworks SDK integration to the Electron launcher (init/restart-app-if-needed, Steam app ID bootstrap), keeping the launcher runnable without Steam during development.
2. Add a "Follow us on Steam" CTA (in launcher UI, e.g. Game Selector screen or settings) that opens the game's Steam store page in the Steam client — candidate mechanisms: `SteamFriends()->ActivateGameOverlayToStore(appId, ...)` in the Steamworks SDK, or `steam://openurl`/`steam://store/<appid>` external URL from Electron.
3. Detect the follow and unlock the bonus game. **Research required:** Steam's client SDK has no direct "user follows this game's store page" call; candidates to verify during implementation:
   - `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(<developer account steamID>)` — client-side check that the user follows the *developer/publisher account* (works without a backend).
   - Steam Web API (`IPlayerService` family, e.g. followed-games queries) — verifies game-page follows but needs a server component and publisher API key.
   - Whichever mechanism is chosen must be verified against the actual Steam account model (game-page follow vs developer-account follow) before committing.
4. Unlock persistence: store a local unlock flag (or Steam-follow state) so the player isn't re-prompted; re-check on demand (e.g. "Refresh" or on follow confirmation).
5. Graceful degradation when Steam/Steamworks is absent: CTA hidden or browser fallback; web app unaffected.
6. Tests + docs: mock Steamworks session for automated unlock-logic tests where feasible; manual end-to-end QA with a real Steam account documented in the test plan.

## Key Files

- `electron/main.ts` (new) — Steamworks init, Steam app ID bootstrap, store-page open handler, follow-check orchestration.
- `electron/steam-follow.ts` (new) — follow detection + unlock persistence logic (game-agnostic), behind a small interface so the web renderer doesn't depend on the Steam SDK directly.
- `electron/preload.ts` (new) — expose a minimal follow/unlock API to the renderer via context bridge.
- `src/ui/` or launcher UI module — "Follow us on Steam" CTA component (SLL-compliant placement), unlock state display.
- `package.json` — Steamworks SDK dependency (or native module) and scripts; electron-builder config for the Steam distribution.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md`, `RELEASE.md` — document the Steamworks build/QA workflow.
- `AGENTS.md` — note new scripts/requirements if tooling changes.
- `tests/` — unit tests for unlock/persistence logic with a mocked follow source; manual E2E test plan for real-Steam verification.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW – Electron launcher for a Steam-ready binary release** (open, intake_complete) — prerequisite: the launcher this feature extends. Its AC #4 (DLC/content-location architecture) must be honored; this feature introduces the deferred Steamworks scope.
- `docs/the-build/genre-research.md` — card-game genre research incl. Steam platform notes (context only).
- No other Steam/Steamworks work items exist (verified via `wl search steam`, `steamworks`, `DLC`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The Steam app (App ID) and developer/publisher Steam account exist outside this repo; this item integrates with them.
- **Assumption:** The designated bonus game is a business decision (TBD — see Appendix) and does not change the technical design (game-agnostic unlock).
- **Assumption:** Following is checked once (on CTA completion) and persisted locally; unfollow-after-unlock is not detected/penalised in v1 (anti-abuse is out of scope).
- **Risk (HIGH):** Steam's client SDK may not expose a reliable client-side "followed this game page" check. Mitigation: implementation begins with a short research spike (candidate APIs above); fallback is developer-account follow via `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing`, or a small web-API verification if acceptable. This may change the UX (e.g. follow developer account instead of game page) — confirm with user before committing to a fallback.
- **Risk:** Steamworks native module adds build complexity to electron-builder packaging and must not break non-Steam dev runs — mitigated by graceful-degradation AC (AC5).
- **Risk:** Electron + Steamworks native module (Steam SDK) packaging on Windows must be validated (steam_appid.txt, app id bootstrap, `SteamAPI_RestartAppIfNecessary`).
- **Scope-creep risk:** Steam overlay for achievements, wishlist prompts, key-distribution systems, and anti-abuse (unfollow detection) are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which game is being released on Steam? The TCE is an engine — are we releasing a specific game built on it (e.g., Main Street), or is this about the engine itself?" — Answer (user): "A launcher with a subset of the example games bundled and the ability to add more later (DLC)." Source: interactive reply. Implication: the Steam "release" is the launcher product (per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW); this item is a mechanic in that launcher.
- Q2: "What's the 'free game' offer? When a player follows, they receive a free game — is that a specific existing game from the TCE catalog, a bonus game, or something else?" — Answer (user): "it will be a game currently in the example games." Source: interactive reply. The specific game title is **not yet chosen (OPEN QUESTION for the business)**; ACs are game-agnostic.
- Q3: "How does the Steam integration work: store page with follow-to-unlock via Steamworks API, manual key-claim flow, or something else?" — Answer (user): "Steam store page via Steamworks." Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "What platform does the launcher target?" — Answer (user): "desktop (we will be using electron, another item covers this, add requirements there if necessary, see CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW)". Source: interactive reply. Decision: Electron stack already scoped in CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW; no requirements added to that item (its scope explicitly defers Steamworks — this feature introduces it and is linked as dependent).
- Q5: "What does 'follow us on Steam' mean technically? Steam has no direct follow webhook..." (options: web flow with in-game store open + API check; code redemption; community group) — Answer (user): "I have played a game that automatically opened the steam store page, I was already logged in and I was following the page. I don't know how they did it, but that's what I want." Source: interactive reply. This is the target UX; the exact Steamworks mechanism is a research spike for implementation (see Risks). Likely components: `ActivateGameOverlayToStore` (or `steam://store/<appid>`) to open the page + a follow-state check.
- OPEN QUESTION: Which example game is the designated free follow-bonus? (business decision; doesn't block technical design — AC4 is game-agnostic.)
- OPEN QUESTION: Follow verification mechanism — game-page follow (needs Steam Web API / backend) vs developer-account follow (`ISteamFriends::IsFollowing`, client-side). Must be researched and confirmed with user before implementation commits to a fallback.

## Related work (automated find-related report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MSI4IP6A000N7YF** – Coloretto: align player collections (hands) regardless of name/score length (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated game feature)*.
- **CG-0MQH81RIS0017K94** – Coloretto Phaser scene (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated)*.
- **CG-0MROXIJZ3004VGUI** – GymTokenPileView: card-back pile shows 'not found' texture (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated)*.

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-...` — the draft itself (self-match).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (+ a worktree copy) — generic terms (game, feature, store); context only, no Steam-specific content.

> Note: The genuinely related item **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW** (Electron launcher) is covered in the manual Related work section above.

# Intake Brief — REFACTOR: break out core engine and individual games into their own projects. (CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17)

## Problem Statement

The Tableau Card Engine is a single flat monorepo where every example game is co-located with the shared engine code. This couples game development to the full repository, makes it hard to version or reuse the engine independently, and prevents building lean distributions that bundle only a selected subset of games.

## Users

- **Engine maintainer (primary)** — Maintains shared engine modules and the Gym demo suite; wants a standalone core-engine repo that can evolve, be versioned, and be pulled into any distribution without dragging all games along.
  - *Story:* As an engine maintainer I can work on `src/core-engine`, `src/card-system`, `src/rule-engine`, `src/ui`, `src/ai` and the Gym in one repo, so that engine changes do not require touching game repos.
- **Game developer** — Builds a single example game in isolation; wants to check out just that game plus the engine and run `npm run dev` / `npm test` / `npm run build` without cloning every other game.
  - *Story:* As a game developer I can clone `tce-golf` (or any game repo) which pulls the core engine as a submodule, so that I can iterate on that game with a fast, focused checkout (`tce-game = distribution with 1 game`).
- **Distribution builder / launcher maintainer** — Assembles and ships a playable bundle (web + desktop binary) that contains the core engine plus a chosen set of 1..n games.
  - *Story:* As a distribution builder I can configure which game submodules are checked out in the launcher repo and run `npm run build` / `npm run package` to produce a web build and an Electron binary that show only the included games in the Game Selector.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Core-engine repo defined and extractable** — A standalone core-engine repository exists (or a concrete extraction plan + script is delivered) containing everything shared across games: `src/core-engine`, `src/card-system`, `src/rule-engine`, `src/ui`, `src/ai`, `src/balance-cards` (if shared), the Gym (`example-games/gym`), the launcher shell (`src/ui/GameSelectorScene`, `src/ui/createCardGame`), Electron launcher (`electron/`), shared assets under `public/assets`, and shared configs (`tsconfig.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `package.json` engine dependencies). Git history for moved files is preserved where feasible.
2. **Per-game repos with reverse submodule** — Each example game (golf, beleaguered-castle, blackjack, sushi-go, feudalism, lost-cities, main-street, coloretto) has its own GitHub repo with a consistent layout that pulls the core engine as a git submodule for standalone development; `npm install`, `npm run dev`, `npm run build`, and `npm test -- --project unit` (or equivalent targeted run) succeed in a `game + engine` checkout and path aliases (`@core-engine/*`, `@card-system/*`, `@rule-engine/*`, `@ui/*`, `@ai/*`) resolve correctly across the submodule boundary. Documented exception: games may vendor only their own `example-games/<game>/` tree.
3. **Launcher distribution assembles N games via submodules** — The main Tableau-Card-Engine repo acts as the launcher/distribution repo: it bundles the core engine plus a configurable set of games checked out as git submodules (e.g. under `games/` or `example-games/`), the Game Selector enumerates only the checked-out games, and `npm run build` (web, `dist/` with `/Tableau-Card-Engine/` base) and `npm run build:electron` / `npm run package` (desktop binary via Electron) succeed for any selection of 1..n games including the boundary cases of 1 game and all games.
4. **Dev workflows and Gym preserved** — `npm run dev` (HMR on port 3000), `vite`/`tsconfig` alias resolution, and the Gym demo scenes all continue to work from the core-engine repo and from the launcher distribution; Gym remains the canonical core-engine feature demonstrator and does not move to a game repo.
5. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
6. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** — `npm run build` succeeds and the relevant test profile passes in the launcher distribution with its default game set (full suite on release; unit + build at minimum before any push per AGENTS.md quality gates).

## Constraints

- Integration mechanism is **git submodules** (option a) — not npm packages or npm workspaces. No npm publication of the engine in this phase.
- **No CI required** in this phase — neither the core-engine repo nor the per-game repos need new GitHub Actions pipelines; existing `pr-checks.yml` / `package.yml` / `deploy.yml` remain on the launcher repo as-is.
- The launcher repo remains the deployable web + Electron distribution; game repos do not deploy independently.
- Preserve permissive-license posture (MIT / CC0) and existing toolchain (Phaser 4 RC, TypeScript strict, Vite, Vitest, Electron).
- Avoid breaking existing developer workflows more than necessary; submodule setup must be documented with copy-paste commands (`git clone --recurse-submodules`, `git submodule update --init --recursive`).
- Keep changes surgical — do not speculatively introduce versioning, changelogs, or release automation beyond what is needed to make the submodule composition build.

## Existing State

- Flat monorepo with a single `package.json` (v0.1.15), single `vite.config.ts` (path aliases for `@core-engine`, `@card-system`, `@rule-engine`, `@ui`, `@ai`), single `tsconfig.json`, and single `index.html` / `main.ts` unified entry point that hard-imports every game scene and registers them in `GAMES` for `GameSelectorScene`.
- Shared engine code under `src/` (`core-engine`, `card-system`, `rule-engine`, `ui`, `ai`, `balance-cards`); example games under `example-games/` (gym, golf, beleaguered-castle, blackjack, sushi-go, feudalism, lost-cities, main-street, coloretto); Gym is the interactive demo suite for core-engine features.
- Electron launcher under `electron/` with `build:electron` / `start:electron` / `package` scripts; `.gitmodules` does not exist; production build targets GitHub Pages at `/Tableau-Card-Engine/` and desktop binaries via `electron-builder`.
- Tests under `tests/` with Vitest projects (unit, browser, smoke, dev, tutorial E2E); game scenes and core modules are tightly coupled via static imports in `main.ts`.

## Desired Change

- Extract a **core-engine repository** that owns all shared code plus Gym and the launcher shell (GameSelector, Electron host). The extraction should be reproducible and preserve history (e.g. via `git filter-repo` / `git subtree` or a documented manual move — exact tooling is an implementation detail but must be recorded).
- Move each **example game to its own GitHub repo** (one repo per game, consistent layout). Each game repo composes a runnable project by pulling the core engine as a git submodule — i.e. a game checkout is itself a minimal TCE distribution with 1 game. Submodule pointer + local Vite/TS configs make engine imports resolve without publishing a package.
- Retain the **main Tableau-Card-Engine repo as the launcher/distribution repo** that composes the core engine with any subset of game submodules. Provide a simple mechanism (submodule presence, config file, or CLI flag) to specify which games are included in a given build, so `npm run build` and `npm run package` produce a distribution containing exactly 1..n games (web + binary). The Game Selector must discover games dynamically from the checked-out set rather than hardcoding all imports.
- Update docs (`README.md`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `public/assets/CREDITS.md` where relevant) and add submodule setup / distribution-build instructions. No new CI or npm publishing is required in this phase.

## Key Files

- `package.json` — Split / slim per-repo manifests; launcher and game repos need correct deps and scripts (`dev`, `build`, `build:electron`, `package`, `test`).
- `vite.config.ts` — Alias resolution must work across submodule boundaries; launcher needs dynamic game discovery instead of static imports.
- `tsconfig.json` — Path aliases and `include` paths must cover submodule layouts.
- `main.ts` — Unified entry point / GameSelector registration; must become dynamic (enumerate checked-out games rather than hardcoding all scenes).
- `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts` — Game catalogue / registry (`REGISTRY_KEY_GAMES`); needs to handle a variable game set.
- `src/core-engine/**`, `src/card-system/**`, `src/rule-engine/**`, `src/ui/**`, `src/ai/**`, `src/balance-cards/**` — Shared engine code that stays in core.
- `example-games/gym/**` — Stays in core as the engine feature demonstrator.
- `example-games/<game>/**` — Each moves to its own repo (golf, beleaguered-castle, blackjack, sushi-go, feudalism, lost-cities, main-street, coloretto).
- `electron/**` — Launcher host; stays in core/launcher, must build against the composed distribution.
- `public/assets/**` — Shared card/back assets stay in core; game-specific assets move with their game or are documented as shared vs. game-owned.
- `index.html` — Entry HTML; must work in both core-only and composed builds.
- `.gitmodules` (new) — Submodule declarations for launcher→games and game→core compositions.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md` — Require updates for new repo layout, submodule workflows, and distribution builds.
- `scripts/**` — Build/test helpers (e.g. `run-ci-tests.sh`, `vite-transcript-plugin.ts`, `build-electron-main.mjs`) may need path adjustments.

## Related Work

- **Potentially related work items:**
  - `Scaffold Card Game Engine project (CG-0MLSFU7300TLFCBH)` — completed — established the current flat-monorepo structure, toolchain, and path aliases that this refactor will decompose.
  - `Create a Gym (CG-0MP3XQBL4008QK8S)` — completed — Gym is the canonical core-engine demonstrator that must remain in the core repo per producer direction.
- **Potentially related docs (paths):**
  - `README.md` — repo layout, quick-start, deployment model.
  - `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — project structure, path aliases, adding a game, building/packaging.
  - `AGENTS.md` — monorepo layout, SLL requirement, quality gates, worklog rules; needs updating for the new multi-repo model.
  - `vite.config.ts` / `tsconfig.json` — alias and build configuration that must span submodules.
  - `main.ts` / `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts` — current static game registration that must become dynamic.
  - `electron/launcher-config.ts` / `electron/content-locator.ts` — desktop content resolution for the launcher.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Submodule ergonomics** — Git submodules are notoriously easy to misuse (detached HEAD, forgotten `--recurse-submodules`). *Mitigation:* document exact clone/update commands, add a `scripts/setup.sh` or `npm run setup` helper if helpful, and keep the default launcher checkout including a known-good game set.
- **History preservation vs. effort** — Preserving full git history for moved files adds complexity (`filter-repo`/`subtree`). *Assumption:* history preservation is preferred but not blocking — a well-documented move with a single squashed history is acceptable if tooling proves too heavy; record the decision in the implementation plan.
- **Dynamic GameSelector discovery** — Replacing static imports with dynamic discovery (filesystem or manifest) may require Vite glob imports or a small codegen step. *Mitigation:* prototype the discovery mechanism early; keep a fallback static list for the initial cut.
- **Asset ownership ambiguity** — Some assets under `public/assets/` are shared vs. game-specific. *Mitigation:* audit `public/assets/CREDITS.md` and per-game asset usage; move only clearly game-owned assets with their game.
- **Scope creep** — Versioning, npm publishing, per-game CI, and release automation are natural follow-ons but are explicitly **out of scope** for this epic. *Mitigation:* file them as separate follow-up work items rather than expanding this one.
- **Assumption:** No CI or npm publication is required in this phase (per producer). Web + binary builds from the launcher are sufficient validation.
- **Assumption:** Core engine contains "everything shared across games" — includes `balance-cards` and the launcher shell; Gym stays in core (per producer).

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "How should the core engine be consumed by individual game repos? (a) git submodule/subtrees, (b) npm package, or (c) monorepo workspaces?" — Answer (producer, this session): "(a) git submodule/subtrees." Source: interactive reply to intake interview Q1. Research: inspected `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `.gitmodules` (absent), `main.ts` static imports, `electron/` layout — confirmed current flat monorepo with no submodules or workspaces.
- Q: "What stays vs. what moves — which components belong in the standalone core-engine repo? Does Gym stay in core?" — Answer (producer, this session): "core engine contains everything that is shared across games, gym remains in the core." Source: interactive reply to intake interview Q2. Research: listed `src/` (`core-engine`, `card-system`, `rule-engine`, `ui`, `ai`, `balance-cards`), `example-games/` (8 games + gym), `public/assets/` — confirmed Gym is under `example-games/gym` and shared modules are under `src/`.
- Q: "How should builds and deployments change — CI, versioning, npm publication, per-game deploys, launcher assembly?" — Answer (producer, this session): "no CI, or npm publication yet but we do want to be able to build a web and binary distribution that includes a specified set of games, no CI in the games either, Yes main repo is a launcher." Source: interactive reply to intake interview Q3. Research: inspected `package.json` scripts (`build`, `build:electron`, `package`, `package:win/linux/mac`), `vite.config.ts` base handling for Pages vs. Electron, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` deployment section — confirmed current GitHub Pages + Electron packaging from the monorepo.

## Foundational Test-References

- `tests/gym/GymSceneSmoke.browser.test.ts` — Gym smoke coverage (must keep passing from core/launcher).
- `tests/smoke.phaser4.browser.test.ts` — Phaser 4 smoke.
- `tests/vite-config.test.ts` — Vite alias / build config coverage.
- `tests/electron/launch-smoke.test.ts` — Electron launcher smoke.
- Full suite (`npm test` / `npm run build`) — release gate for the launcher distribution with its default game set.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MTHTJLES009CRHQ** – Linter auto-fix: engine modules (completed)
- **CG-0MP2988UN009P9LM** – Extract shared HUD layer into core engine and adopt across games (completed)
- **CG-0MQN1BLHH0086LU8** – F2: ActiveEffect infrastructure in state & serialization (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: able, around, break, building, bundled (+23 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: able, break, building, card, core (+17 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: able, break, building, card, core (+17 more)

# Park should cost 40 coins (0.4) per turn to maintain

## Summary

Give the Main Street **Park** (`cs-park`) community-space card a per-turn running cost, so that placing a Park is no longer a free, costless synergy anchor. The producer directive reads "Park should cost 0.4 per turn to maintain"; because the economy is now integer-only (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6, ×100 rescale), the faithful value is **40 coins/turn**.

## Problem statement

The Park is the cheapest Tier-1 community space (cost 300) and currently has **no ongoing cost** (`ongoingCost` empty → 0). Playtest notes describe Park-spam ("Two Parks provide cheap Culture filler"; "The Culture-heavy cluster … generates massive synergy income") with no downside. The producer wants a maintenance cost so Parks impose a real per-turn drain and spamming them is a meaningful trade-off.

## Users

- **Player** — builds a Park-heavy Entertainment/Culture cluster and should feel the ongoing cash drain as a real strategic cost.
- **Producer / balance owner** — wants Park to stop being a free synergy anchor and to have a lever to curb Park spam.

Example user stories:

- As a player, when I place a Park on the street I want to see that it costs me coins each turn, so I can weigh Park spam against my coin income.
- As a balance owner, I want the Park's running cost to appear in the card data, tooltip and card face so the cost is transparent and testable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Card data** — `cs-park` in `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` has `ongoingCost = 40` (the integer-economy equivalent of the specified 0.4/turn after the ×100 rescale, CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6).
2. **IncomePhase deduction** — at end of turn, each placed, **unsold** Park deducts 40 coins through the existing `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts()` path, alongside other community-space/staff/business costs, clamped at 0 coins and logged ("Community space costs: -N coins …") with an insufficient-funds log when the bank cannot cover it.
3. **Tooltip** — the Park community-space tooltip includes the ongoing-cost line `Ongoing cost: -40/turn` (auto-derived from `ongoingCost`); the Park description in `card-data.csv` states the running cost, matching the Library/Community Garden wording ("Costs 40 coins per turn to run.").
4. **Card face** — the street/market card overlay for a Park displays the 40 coin/turn cost in the two-tone cash line (the existing community-space overlay path, CG-0MTCP76MP0088TQW/CG-0MTDMOYOL008IQVO — no baked SVG change is expected since community-space ongoing cost was removed from the baked face).
5. **Sold-card exemption preserved** — a sold Park incurs no ongoing cost (existing CG-0MU3VH7QW006A2XA behaviour), verified by test.
6. **Tests** — existing Park assumptions are updated (`tests/main-street/community-space-ongoing-cost.test.ts` "Park has no ongoing cost" and the mixed sold/unsold case; `tests/main-street/community-space-tooltip.test.ts` "Park tooltip has no ongoing-cost line") and new/updated tests assert the 40/turn deduction, the tooltip line, clamping/insufficient-funds, and the sold-card exemption. Each test asserts a distinct behaviour (no redundant duplicates).
7. **Balance sanity** — the tutorial scenario (verified: it places no Park — its scripted market is Bakery/Laundromat/Festival) and the Monte Carlo balance guardrails remain green (or any drift is measured and reported in the work item); no guardrail band is silently widened.
8. **Docs** — `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` (Park's `Ongoing/turn` column 0 → 40) and `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (that table has no Ongoing column, so Park's row gains the "Costs 40 coins per turn to run." sentence, matching the Library row) are updated; any other doc that lists Park's ongoing cost (e.g. `core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `balancing-methodology.md`) is checked and updated to 40 coins/turn; stale pre-rescale rows (e.g. `the-build-gdd.md` Park-as-business) are corrected or explicitly flagged.
9. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
10. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Integer economy (hard):** coins/reputation are whole integers (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6). The literal value `0.4` rounds to `0` via `roundInt()` and is not a viable ongoing cost; it must be expressed as `40`. Do not reintroduce fractional coin values or per-card rounding.
- **Data is source of truth:** ongoing cost lives in `card-data.csv`; the tooltip, overlay and deduction all derive from it. No hard-coded Park cost elsewhere.
- **Charging semantics unchanged:** ongoing costs apply only to placed cards, exclude sold slots, and are clamped at 0 coins — Park must reuse the existing community-space mechanism, not a new one.
- **Balance values are producer-owned:** the 40 mapping is an agent interpretation, documented as an assumption; it should be easy for the producer to confirm or override.

## Existing state

- `cs-park` (`card-data.csv`): `cost 300`, `baseIncome 0`, `synergyTypes Entertainment`, `reputationPerTurn 0`, `ongoingCost` empty → `0`.
- Deduction engine: `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts()` in `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` sums each placed community-space `ongoingCost`, applies the Cost Cutter street reduction, rounds the **aggregate** via `roundInt()`, clamps the deduction at the coin bank, and logs the cost/shortfall; it skips `soldSlots`.
- Display: community-space tooltip in `MainStreetFormatting.ts` emits `Ongoing cost: -N/turn` only when `ongoingCost > 0`; the horizontal `+X / -Y` card-overlay cash line is built in `UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` and rendered by `MainStreetRendererStreet.ts`. Community-space ongoing cost is deliberately **not** baked into the card SVG.
- Tests currently assert the opposite (`Park has no ongoing cost`, `Park tooltip has no ongoing-cost line`).
- Historical truth: the pre-×100 economy had Park `ongoing = empty`; Library `0.25`, Community Garden `0.1`, Health Kiosk `0.15`, Public Art `0.25`. Commit `192943c9` (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6) scaled these ×100 to 25/10/15/25, so `0.4 → 40`.

## Desired change

1. Set `cs-park.ongoingCost = 40` in `card-data.csv` and add the running-cost sentence to Park's description.
2. Update the tests that encode "Park is free", add explicit 40/turn coverage, and verify the tooltip line and sold-card exemption.
3. Update the balance/design docs that list Park's ongoing cost.
4. Confirm the Park card overlay shows the 40/turn cost and that tutorials/balance guardrails are unaffected (or report measured drift).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — set `cs-park` `ongoingCost` to `40` and update the description text.
- `tests/main-street/community-space-ongoing-cost.test.ts` — update "Park has no ongoing cost" and the mixed sold/unsold Park case; add Park deduction + clamping + sold-exemption coverage.
- `tests/main-street/community-space-tooltip.test.ts` — replace "Park tooltip has no ongoing-cost line" with an assertion that the tooltip contains `Ongoing cost: -40/turn`.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — Park row gains the 40 coins/turn running-cost note (the community-space table has no Ongoing column) and a rationale note.
- `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` — community-space table Park ongoing 0 → 40.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — revise any Park-ongoing statement / examples.
- `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` — note Park's new running cost (community-space curve excludes `ongoingCost`).
- `docs/main-street/the-build-gdd.md` — Park row currently lists a stale no-cost entry (verify/update).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — expected **no change** (already generic over `ongoingCost > 0`); verify only.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` / `MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — expected **no change** (generic cash line); verify Park shows `-40`.

## Related work

- CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6 — integer economy ×100 rescale (defines the 0.4 → 40 conversion).
- CG-0MU3VH7QW006A2XA — sold cards excluded from ongoing costs (Park must keep this behaviour).
- CG-0MSVYPEZ90085SHE — business ongoing-cost rebalance (precedent for the ongoing-cost mechanic and tooltip/overlay display).
- CG-0MRXYGM9B006I3PE — community-space ongoing-cost / Library repurposing (the mechanic Park will use; "Park model" synergy participation).
- CG-0MQBLGQ2Z0066UGP — "Park is not a business" reclassification (`cs-park` identity).
- CG-0MTR39XO6002CBB1 — open: "Events income/costs should be shown on the business cards" (card-cost display surface).
- Original source: ContextHub WL-0MTH6O957004963U (deleted; transferred here).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (value):** "0.4" is in the pre-×100 scale, so the current-economy value is **40** coins/turn. Evidence: the requirement pre-dates commit `192943c9` (2026-09-02), which scaled every `ongoingCost` ×100, and the engine rounds to integers. **Producer should confirm 40.** If the producer instead wants a literal sub-1 cost, the integer economy must be revisited (out of scope here).
- **Balance drift risk:** Park is a Tier-1 card used by tutorials and Park-spam playtests; a 40/turn cost can shift tutorial economy and Monte Carlo guardrails. Mitigation: run the relevant tutorial/balance tests and report any drift rather than silently widening bands.
- **Correctness risk:** a naive change could double-charge or break the sold-slot exemption. Mitigation: rely on the existing `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts()` path and cover it with tests.
- **Doc drift risk:** Park's ongoing cost appears in several docs; missing one leaves stale guidance. Mitigation: grep all Park/ongoing references as part of the change.
- **Scope-creep risk:** re-tuning other community spaces (e.g. Playground or Fountain also have no cost) is a separate balance decision — capture any such opportunity as its own linked work item, not in this change.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The original ContextHub intake was blocked on producer questions. Those are now resolved from repository evidence (the item description notes agents on this project can resolve them directly):

- **Q (original): What project/domain does `park` belong to, and which codebase needs the change?**
  — **Answer (agent, from repo evidence):** Tableau-Card-Engine, Main Street game. The target is the `cs-park` community-space card. Source: ContextHub audit comment on WL-0MTH6O957004963U; `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv`. Resolution of original Q1/Q2/Q5.

- **Q (original): What is a `park` and what is a `turn` in this context?**
  — **Answer (agent, from repo evidence):** `Park` is the Tier-1 Main Street community-space card `cs-park`; a `turn` is a Main Street turn whose end-of-turn IncomePhase deducts ongoing costs. Source: `MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts`, `MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts()`. Resolution of original Q2/Q3.

- **Q (original): What is the current behaviour and cost?**
  — **Answer (agent, from repo evidence):** Park has no ongoing cost (`ongoingCost` empty → 0); tests assert "Park has no ongoing cost" and "Park tooltip has no ongoing-cost line". Source: `card-data.csv`, `tests/main-street/community-space-ongoing-cost.test.ts:179`, `tests/main-street/community-space-tooltip.test.ts:200`. Resolution of original Q4.

- **Q: What does "0.4 per turn" mean in the current integer economy?**
  — **Answer (agent, from repo evidence):** **40 coins/turn.** The directive pre-dates the ×100 integer-economy conversion (commit `192943c9`, 2026-09-02, CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6), which scaled every `ongoingCost` ×100 (Library `0.25 → 25`, Community Garden `0.1 → 10`, Health Kiosk `0.15 → 15`, Public Art `0.25 → 25`). `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts()` rounds the aggregate with `roundInt()`, so a literal `0.4` rounds to `0` and is not representable. Source: `git show 192943c9`, `git show 192943c9^:example-games/main-street/card-data.csv`, `MainStreetDifficulty.ts#roundInt`.

- **OPEN QUESTION (for producer confirmation, not blocking):** is 40 coins/turn the intended post-rescale value, or should Park's cost be a different integer? The agent proceeds with 40 as the documented interpretation; the producer may override this single value.

# Documentation gap — stale game paths in `docs/DEVELOPER.md`

**discovered-from:CG-0MUMAIIT40002MRP** (Update AGENTS.md for the split multi-repo structure and cross-repo change guidance)

## Problem

`docs/DEVELOPER.md` documents the **merged core checkout** (`Tableau-Card-Engine`) but still lists example-game paths as `example-games/<game>/…` for games that now live in sibling `tce-<game>` repos at repo-root `src/`. This was discovered while correcting the equivalent stale paths in `AGENTS.md`; it is out of scope for that item (which is bounded to `AGENTS.md` + the context-budget threshold).

## Evidence

`grep -nE 'example-games/(golf|blackjack|coloretto|main-street|sushi-go|feudalism|lost-cities|beleaguered-castle)' docs/DEVELOPER.md` returns roughly 40 non-Gym references, including:

- **Game reference table** — `example-games/golf/`, `example-games/main-street/`, `example-games/beleaguered-castle/`, etc.
- **Hand & Pile Rendering** — `example-games/golf/scenes/GolfRenderer.ts`, `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts`.
- **Animation & Sound Feedback** — `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoAiScheduler.ts`, `example-games/golf/scenes/GolfAnimator.ts`, `example-games/blackjack/scenes/BlackjackScene.ts`.
- **SLL layout table / Main Street asset generation / Renderer migration / tutorial paths** — further `example-games/main-street/…` references.

The multi-repo note at the top of the *Project Structure* section already states the core carries no games at HEAD and that each game lives at repo-root `src/`, so the file is internally contradictory.

## Desired change

Repoint every non-Gym game path in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` to the sibling layout (`../tce-<game>/src/…`), or to the game repo's own documented layout where the reference is game-repo-relative. Gym references (`example-games/gym/…`) stay unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `grep -nE 'example-games/(golf|blackjack|coloretto|main-street|sushi-go|feudalism|lost-cities|beleaguered-castle)' docs/DEVELOPER.md` returns no matches; remaining `example-games/` references are Gym-only or structural.
2. No code/behaviour change (docs only).
3. Build and the unit test profile pass.
4. Relevant doc cross-links (e.g. `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`, `README.md`) remain consistent.

## Constraints

- Docs-only change; write UK English; no new top-level doc structure.

## Summary

**Status: awaiting operator execution (2026-09-30).** The agent cannot run this: it needs a **Windows x64 host with a real Steam client and account**, which is not provisioned in the agent environment. 1. On Windows x64: `npm install steamworks.js && npm run build:steam-friends && npm run package:steam`.
